title: Sharding/Partitioning on Monotonically Increasing Key modulo N (Hash Mod N)
pattern: Mapping a primary or routing key to a database node or partition using direct modulo arithmetic (`hash(key) % N`).
why_bad: Rebalancing is catastrophically expensive. When the number of nodes $N$ changes (e.g., scaling up from 10 to 11), almost every key's target partition changes ($123456 \pmod{10} = 6$ vs. $123456 \pmod{11} = 3$), forcing a massive, expensive data migration across the entire cluster [157, 158].
detection: Database routing code or partition index calculation using raw modulo arithmetic on a variable node count.
counterexample: Modulo on a fixed, unchangeable number of virtual partitions (which are then mapped to nodes).
fix: Use consistent hashing or a fixed number of logical partitions assigned to physical nodes.
